property_summary: After any winning play (random==0), the pot must be paid out and reset to zero; the mutant leaves pot non-zero after a win, so asserting pot==0 after a winning round distinguishes them.

For any sequence of admissible plays, c.pot() must equal the sum of successful deposits minus all winnings already paid out (i.e., the pot is reduced to zero on every winning play); the mutant fails to reset the pot after a win, so its pot drifts above the accounted expectation.

Because the pot resets to zero after every winning round, a player who wins immediately after another winner must be paid exactly TICKET_AMOUNT - FEE_AMOUNT (9 wei); the mutant, never resetting the pot, pays the second winner 19 wei instead, breaking the rule for some inputs.

For every successful play, the pot must be either 0 (a win: bank takes the fee and the player drains the pot, leaving pot reset to 0) or the full ticket amount 10 (a loss); the mutant leaves pot at 1 after a win, violating this rule.
After any winning play (random == 0), the pot is fully reset to zero; the mutant leaves pot at FEE_AMOUNT = 1, so some winning input breaks the invariant that a win empties the pot.

After any call to play, either the call reverts or the pot is exactly 0 (a winning play fully drains the pot) or 10 (a losing play just added the ticket); the mutant leaves pot = 1 after a win, violating this for some winning (warp, actor) input.
